0.long_answer: Dup15q syndrome, also known as Chromosome 15q duplication syndrome, is a rare genetic disorder resulting from an extra copy of genetic material on the long arm of chromosome 15. This extra material is typically present as an isodicentric chromosome or marker chromosome, which leads to partial tetrasomy of the 15q11.2-q13.1 region. The duplication of this critical region affects the expression of several genes that are important for neurological development, contributing to intellectual disabilities, developmental delays, hypotonia, and an increased risk for autism spectrum disorders. The severity and specific symptoms of Dup15q syndrome can vary among individuals, depending on the size and location of the duplication, as well as the number of gene copies present.
